descriptionMarkdown:
Characters can recover enemy equipment, but a battlefield is not a consequence-free catalogue. Salvage bypasses the 
question of whether the item physically exists; it does not bypass condition, ammunition, legality, compatibility, 
ownership or maintenance.
Step Player Procedure
1. Secure
The item must actually be recovered from 
the scene. A retreat, collapsing site or 
hostile reinforcements can make this 
impossible.
2. Assess
Use Investigation, Technology or an 
appropriate tool proficiency when the item's 
condition, traps, corruption or unfamiliar 
technology is uncertain.
3. Restore
Damaged or Worn gear may require parts, a 
maintenance kit, workshop time or a project 
before it can be trusted.
4. Integrate
Unfamiliar, species-pattern, Mechanicus, 
xenos or proscribed gear may require 
training, an interface, ammunition or a 
specialist before use.
5. Explain
If authorities care about ownership or 
legality, the warband needs a believable 
provenance, permit, patron or very 
convincing lie.
Recovering an item therefore does not require a normal Requisition test, but keeping it may create an equivalent cost in 
repairs, contacts, Heat, favours or narrative risk. This is deliberate: loot should create choices rather than convert every 
battlefield into a shopping trip.
